text.zh: 头顶是玻璃和铁搭成的巨大车棚。在当时，这是最现代的建筑。
text.en: Overhead is a huge shed of glass and iron, the most modern kind of building at the time.

text.zh: 火车头升起的蒸汽，被困在车棚里翻滚。
text.en: Steam rising from the locomotives is trapped inside the shed.

text.zh: 日光从屋顶大片的玻璃透进来，和蒸汽混在一起。莫奈最着迷的，正是这种人工和自然效果的组合。
text.en: Daylight pours through the great glazed sections of the roof and mixes with the steam. It was this combination of artificial and natural effects that fascinated Monet.

text.zh: 印象派最前卫的一点，是画现代的工业化巴黎：铁桥、展览馆、火车站。
text.en: One of the most avant-garde things about the Impressionists was their choice of modern, industrial Paris as a subject: iron bridges, exhibition halls, train stations.

text.zh: 1877年1月，他开始画这个车站，大约四个月就画了12幅。
text.en: In January 1877 he began painting this station, and completed twelve paintings in about four months.

text.zh: 今天，这幅画挂在奥赛博物馆，而奥赛本身就是一座改建的火车站。
text.en: Today the painting hangs in the Musée d'Orsay, which is itself a converted railway station.

exclusive._说明: 独家发现“同一个车站，另一种样子”：对比滑块，左边是奥赛这一幅，右边是芝加哥艺术博物馆的《诺曼底火车进站》（CC0，images/normandy-train.jpg，Tia 上传）。打开就算发现了卡片“十二幅”。

title.zh: 第一幕 · 巴黎最繁忙的车站

text.zh: 1877年1月，莫奈开始画圣拉扎尔火车站，当时巴黎最大、最繁忙的车站。大约四个月里，他画了12幅。
text.en: In January 1877, Monet began painting the Gare Saint-Lazare, then the largest and busiest station in Paris. In about four months, he painted twelve views.

alt.zh: 莫奈《圣拉扎尔火车站》1877年，巴黎奥赛博物馆
alt.en: Claude Monet, The Saint-Lazare Station, 1877, Musée d'Orsay, Paris

text.zh: 那年4月，他在第三届印象派画展上展出了其中好几幅。作家左拉称赞他画出了现代火车站的兴奋和活力。同一场画展上，还有卡耶博特的《巴黎街道，雨天》。
text.en: That April, he showed several of them at the third Impressionist exhibition. The writer Émile Zola praised him for capturing the excitement and energy of the modern station. At the same exhibition was Caillebotte's *Paris Street; Rainy Day*.

alt.zh: 莫奈《圣拉扎尔火车站》1877年，巴黎奥赛博物馆
alt.en: Claude Monet, The Saint-Lazare Station, 1877, Musée d'Orsay, Paris

title.zh: 第三幕 · 最后一次画城市

text.zh: 这组车站画开启了莫奈一生的做法：一次又一次画同一个主题，捕捉光线的变化。但这也是他最后一次画城市生活，从此以后，他几乎只画风景。
text.en: This group of station paintings began a lifelong habit for Monet: painting the same subject again and again to capture the changing light. But it was also his last attempt to paint city life. From then on, he devoted himself almost entirely to landscape.
